title: What Comes After Games
coreClaim: Berne named three qualities that together constitute autonomy: awareness (direct perception rather than filtered), spontaneity (response from the appropriate ego state rather than the habitual one), and intimacy (game-free contact between two people both free of their patterns). None is a technique. They are what remains when the structures around them are slowly, imperfectly dismantled.

anchorsUsed.name: Solenne
anchorsUsed.description: Solenne notices her pre-formed defensive explanation in her throat before she decides to say it, watching it from a small distance for three seconds.

anchorsUsed.name: Casimir and Valeria
anchorsUsed.description: Casimir asks 'Tell me what starting looks like when it goes wrong' instead of explaining again; the question surprises him as much as Valeria.

anchorsUsed.name: Takeshi and Fenna
anchorsUsed.description: A Saturday coffee conversation in March where neither is running a pattern on the other and both are present with what the other is actually saying.

hardDepthTension: Each quality has a failure mode: awareness collapses into observation-as-practice (a new script), spontaneity collapses into compulsive reaction (a new default), intimacy collapses into structural imitation (a pattern mimicking game-free contact). The triad is available but not installable. The threshold question (is naming it worth doing if rarely reached?) is answered by pointing out that naming a direction is not the same as promising arrival.
strongestQualities: Solenne opening scene earns its position by delivering awareness-before-vocabulary in a recognizable moment.
Failure mode for each quality named with structural precision without moralizing.
P7 closes the ten-chapter arc cleanly without opening a new question.
The triad's connection to Ch4's debt named in hard depth without disrupting prose flow.
remainingConcerns: None. Medium competitive (330 words) is at the minimum of the allowed range but within bounds.
